causal_conclusion: Raw external supply is not the dominant blocker.

Two independent viable executable suppliers are admitted but buried below the top-50 cutoff because they carry only one domain/format lexical match while unrelated or auxiliary candidates accumulate multiple generic matches.

One viable supplier is absent from the admitted pool even though raw apt-cache search returns it, proving exact token admission can also discard capability-relevant packages whose metadata uses different wording.
The common structural weakness is that package-name/short-description lexical overlap is being treated as capability evidence even when it does not encode the executable's actual operation.

repair_eligibility.scope_boundary: A generic retention/ranking repair may address repeated below-cutoff loss. The single mediainfo non-admission event is evidence but does not alone authorize a separate task-specific admission repair.

next_action.objective: Search existing zero-cost metadata sources that expose package executable names/capabilities (for example package contents/manpage/command metadata) and measure whether they recover operation-level evidence for the known buried/missed suppliers before inventing a new ranking algorithm.
next_action.rationale: The winning repair should enrich capability evidence rather than merely retune lexical weights.
